headline: Urban woodlands ordinance advances, requiring permits to remove five or more mature trees
summary: The ordinance would cover parcels of 5,000 square feet or more with 10 or more private shade trees or 25% tree canopy, and it returns to committee before final action. A new seven-member Urban Woodlands Commission would issue permits, and violators would face a $300 penalty per tree removed. Shelter residents spoke during public comment about conditions at Friends of the Homeless and CSO on Worthington Street. Members also passed a resolution supporting American International College and sent a cannabis license change at 1300 Boston Road to committee.
decisions: Approved the Springfield Fire Chiefs Association contract, 12-0.
Passed the resolution supporting House Bill 4087 on red light cameras, with 11 yes votes and one abstention.
Approved the September revenue and expenditure report, 11-0.
Approved Eversource petitions on Sherman Street, 1400 State Street, and Barrington Drive, 11-0.
Approved Zayo fiber-optic petitions for Chestnut and Liberty streets, 11-0.
Approved one-way traffic on Edgewood and Sycamore streets and a four-way stop at Washington Street and Commonwealth Avenue, 11-0.
Approved the $55,775.60 municipal road safety grant, 12-0.
Approved the $500,000 grant for the new East Springfield branch, 12-0.
Approved the $1 million grant for the Forest Park Horticultural and Learning Center, 12-0.
Approved the $108,078.74 cable access franchise fee and moved $1 million from stabilization into a tax relief fund, 12-0.
Approved the $36,786,032 bond order for school roof replacements, 12-0.
Referred the Liberty Cannabis host agreement amendment to the General Government Committee, 12-0.
Approved the permanent utility easement for Gerena School, 12-0.
Approved the first step of the urban woodlands ordinance, 12-0.
Approved the resolution supporting American International College, 12-0.
discussion: Friends of the Homeless conditions: Public speakers described cockroaches, unsafe fire exits, poor food, and mistreatment at shelters on Worthington Street, and asked council to investigate. Members said a Health and Human Services committee meeting with Friends of the Homeless would be held.

Urban woodlands ordinance concerns: Members raised questions about the $300 fee per tree, the 10-day and 30-day review periods, and appeals that would go back to the same commission. Those questions are to be discussed in committee before final action.

Flock camera surveillance: A public speaker asked council to ban Flock cameras, citing ACLU records that the speaker said show nearly 1,500 searches that cited immigration enforcement. Members said a new ordinance to ban Flock cameras has been proposed.

Red light camera bill: Rep. Ramos described House Bill 4087, which would let cities opt in to photo enforcement of red light violations, with fines set locally. Rep. Ramos said he will refile the bill in January if it does not pass this session.

American International College future: Members said the college faces financial and accreditation challenges. The college president said enrollment is up slightly, and council plans to meet with the college after Thanksgiving.
